🔔 Ethereum price faces $2,000 test as oil surge revives rate fears 

⚡️ Ethereum price has remained trapped below $2,000 as rising oil prices, renewed interest-rate concerns and BitMEX’s planned shutdown have tempered bullish sentiment despite continued spot ETF inflows. According to data from cryptonews, Ethereum price traded near $1,927 on July 23 after reaching an intraday high of $1,941. The token has recovered more than 27% from its June low near $1,514, but repeated failures around $1,955 have kept the psychological $2,000 level beyond buyers’ reach.

🔗 Rate traders have already adjusted their positions. The probability of a September Fed hike rose to 79% from 68% per data from the CME FedWatch tool. Expectations for the July meeting remain centered on no change, but another oil-led inflation increase could lift Treasury yields and pressure risk assets such as Ethereum. 

🔖 U.S. equities also weakened after Alphabet raised its 2026 capital-spending forecast to between $195 billion and $205 billion. The company recorded negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion as quarterly expenditure doubled to $44.9 billion, while its shares fell in premarket trading.

THE NEXT USER MAY NOT BE HUMAN 🤖

For years, financial platforms were built for people.

A person opened an app.
A person selected an asset.
A person confirmed the transaction.

That model is beginning to change.

AI agents can now receive wallets, pay for digital services, trade assets and complete multi-step financial workflows within limits defined by their owners.

Coinbase reports that its x402 protocol processed more than 160 million agentic payments over the past year. It has also introduced tools that allow AI agents to trade, pay and execute workflows through a connected Coinbase account.

This creates a new type of market participant:

software that can analyse and act without waiting for every individual human command.

But autonomy without control is not intelligence.

Any financial agent needs:

• spending limits
• defined permissions
• approved assets and services
• complete transaction records
• the ability to stop execution immediately

The important question is not:

“Can an AI agent move money?”

It is:

“Under which rules is it allowed to act?”

This is the core principle of systematic finance.

Automation should not operate without boundaries.

It should execute faster inside a clearly defined structure.

The future may belong to autonomous financial agents.
Trust will still depend on the rules controlling them.

📡 Iran-Iraq bond remains unbreakable: Official

📌 Chazabeh, IRNA — The connection between the Iranian and Iraqi nations, forged through their shared devotion to Imam Hossein (PBHU), remains unbreakable, the Governor of Iran’s southwestern Khuzestan Province, Mohammad Reza Mavalizadeh, has said.

Mavalizadeh made the remarks in a meeting with the head of Iraq’s Sheib border crossing on Saturday.
​
Referring to the exemplary solidarity between the Iranian and Iraqi nations during the Arbaeen pilgrimage, he said that the spiritual and historical ties between the Iranian and Iraqi nations, nurtured by their mutual reverence for Imam Hossein (PBHU), are eternal and unbreakable.
​
The establishment of a joint operations room between Iranian and Iraqi officials has played a significant role in streamlining affairs and providing quality services to Arbaeen pilgrims, he added.
​
The joint temporary service stations (Mawkibs) set up by servants of the two countries have displayed a manifestation of unity and brotherhood, he stated.
​
Khuzestan Province, with two official border crossings, Shalamcheh and Chazabeh, is one of the main hubs for Arbaeen pilgrims’ passage in the country.
​
Due to its proximity to the Iraqi border, bilateral cooperation between provincial officials and Iraqi authorities during this period is of particular importance.
​
Shalamcheh border is one of the most important official crossings between Iran and Iraq in Khuzestan Province and serves as a major entry point for pilgrims during Arbaeen.
​
Chazabeh border is also one of Khuzestan’s key crossings on the Iran-Iraq border, receiving large numbers of pilgrims each year during Arbaeen.

Crypto speak: Bull trap

A “bull trap” is a market analysis term that refers to a cryptocurrency’s price action that feigns an impending long-term upward (bullish) trend when, in reality, it’s secretly a short-term correction with more downward pressure.

In other words, if you see a crypto’s price pumping and immediately rush to buy it, congratulations, there’s a strong chance you’re entering a bull trap, and your coin is about to get cheaper 🙃
